title: Global Fintech Fest 2026 Set to Draw 500 Investors as India Cements Fintech Leadership
excerpt: The world's largest fintech conference returns to Mumbai in September, building on last year's landmark edition that drew Modi and Starmer.
body:
• The Global Fintech Fest 2026, scheduled for September 8–10 in Mumbai, is expected to draw about 500 global investors and 400 exhibitors from over 100 countries
  • The event builds on the success of GFF 2025, which saw both Prime Minister Modi and UK Prime Minister Starmer announce the UK-India Fintech Corridor and deepen trade ties
  • Key themes include AI-led financial services, digital public infrastructure, tokenisation, and cross-border fintech partnerships

India's Global Fintech Fest (GFF), billed as the world's largest annual fintech conference, is gearing up for its 2026 edition in Mumbai, with organisers expecting about 500 global investors and 400 exhibitors to converge on the financial capital from September 8 to 10, according to Livemint.

The three-day event, jointly organised by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), the Payments Council of India (PCI), and the Fintech Convergence Council (FCC), will bring together policymakers, regulators, central bankers, fintech companies, startups, and institutional investors from over 100 countries.

Building on a Landmark 2025

The 2026 edition builds on a watershed moment for the conference. Last year's GFF in October drew both Prime Minister Narendra Modi and UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer — marking the first time two sitting heads of government addressed the event together. Starmer arrived with a 126-member delegation, the largest British trade mission to India.

"India constitutes half of the world's digital transactions every day. The India Stack is giving shape to open-source platforms that will provide easy access to credit for small businesses and MSMEs."

— Prime Minister Narendra Modi, GFF 2025

At GFF 2025, the two leaders announced the UK-India Fintech Corridor to pilot and scale startups, and pledged enhanced cooperation between the London Stock Exchange and GIFT City. The Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), which Starmer called "the biggest deal since the UK left the EU," was a centrepiece of the bilateral discussions.

AI and Digital Infrastructure Take Centre Stage

This year's fest is expected to focus heavily on artificial intelligence and its applications in financial services. The Digital India portal, which lists GFF 2026 as a featured government-backed event, describes the conference as a platform where "the movers and shakers of the financial world brainstorm and shape the course of a responsible, sustainable, inclusive, and dynamic global economy, leveraging the latest technological advances, including AI."

The 2025 edition already previewed this shift. At last year's event, Nvidia's India managing director predicted that by 2028, Mumbai would be known as "the financial capital with intelligence" — with AI powering everything from fraud detection to personalised wealth advisory in local languages.

Conference Chairman Kris Gopalakrishnan has framed the event as a thought leadership platform aimed at reshaping finance to be "more inclusive, agile, and resilient." Over a dozen central banks, including regulators from Germany, France, Switzerland, and Singapore, are expected to attend.

Why It Matters for the Diaspora

For NRI tech professionals and investors, GFF reflects the maturation of India's fintech ecosystem into a global force. India's unified payments interface (UPI) now processes billions of transactions monthly, and the country's digital public infrastructure — Aadhaar, UPI, and the India Stack — has become a model studied by governments worldwide.

The bilateral India-UK trade relationship, currently valued at approximately $56 billion with a target of doubling by 2030, creates direct opportunities for diaspora professionals working across both markets. The fintech corridor announced at GFF 2025 is designed to facilitate cross-border startup scaling and regulatory alignment.

What's Next

GFF 2026 arrives at a moment of rapid evolution in global financial technology. Agentic AI, tokenised assets, and embedded finance are reshaping how financial services are built and delivered. With India processing half the world's digital transactions daily and its fintech sector attracting growing global capital, the Mumbai conference has become a bellwether for the industry's direction.

Registration details and the full speaker lineup are expected on the official Global Fintech Fest website in the coming weeks.
